notes:
The last unreadable document in this source, recovered: 77000334, the Mills Building and Tower nomination, for which npgallery.nps.gov serves only a placeholder ("The PDF file for this National Register record has not yet been digitized"). The scan was found in the National Archives catalog's digitized National Register records for California ("California SP Mills Building and Tower", NAID 123861210), which carries a text layer. 12 pages, the 10-300 form prepared by the San Francisco Landmarks Preservation Advisory Board in February 1976 and certified 13 April 1977. Its section 7 is mostly a quoted San Francisco Chronicle article of 13 October 1890 announcing construction; section 8 gives the construction and alteration history.

The other undigitized listing, 01000281 (San Francisco Maritime National Historic Site, certified 27 June 1988), is not recoverable this way: its NARA file (NAID 123861287) contains only the WASO locator card — the nomination folder itself is missing from the archive's holdings. It is recorded here as a stub and stays needs-human.

Citations in this batch point at the NARA scan, since the npgallery URL serves a placeholder rather than the document.

findings.description: Built to a design by the Chicago firm Burnham and Root, mostly the work of John Wellborn Root — a ten-storey steel-frame office building, one of the city's first three steel-framed buildings and the only one of them that has survived.

extra.architect: Burnham and Root (design mostly John Wellborn Root)

citation.label: National Register of Historic Places nomination, Mills Building and Tower (reference number 77000334), National Park Service, via the National Archives catalog.

raw.text: SPECIFIC DATES 1890 / BUILDER/ARCHITECT Burnham and Root ... it was designed in 1890 by Burnham and Root, a Chicago firm. Of the first three steel frame buildings in the city, only the Mills Building remains ... Most of the design was apparently the work of Root

resolution.method: EAS exact match on 220 MONTGOMERY ST → parcel 0268008; sf-parcels has blklot 0268008 active, 270–276 BUSH; the 2025 roll records it as commercial office, built 1900. EAS puts 200, 216, 220, 232 MONTGOMERY ST on that parcel, so per the directory contract the fact belongs on one page at the lowest, 200. The record was written in 1977, after the 1909 renumbering, so the number it gives is a modern number and the renumbering guard does not apply; the assessor dates the building on this parcel to 1900.
